dedupe_keys.name: voxcity voxel based 3d city model generator and environmental simulator

description: VoxCity is an open Python framework that builds voxel-based three-dimensional city models from open geospatial data and runs simple environmental simulations on them. It covers generation of building heights, tree canopy heights, land cover and terrain for a chosen area anywhere on Earth from open sources, and simulation of solar irradiance, sky and green view indices and landmark visibility on the resulting model; the paper demonstrates 8 cities. It was developed by Kunihiko Fujiwara and co-authors and described in arXiv 2504.13934 (April 2025). The code is available from the GitHub repository and as a PyPI package (version 1.6.3, August 2026) under the MIT licence, free of charge; models can be exported to ENVI-met INX input files for microclimate simulation and to PALM static drivers and OBJ meshes. Caveats: the quality of the model depends on the open data available for each place, and many data sources are served through Google Earth Engine, which needs an account. It is useful for preparing city geometry with trees and green cover for heat, microclimate and green infrastructure studies and for digital twin prototypes; a related record is the Copernicus Urban Atlas.
